questions.question: Explain how rain becomes a flood, using the terms infiltration, surface run-off and saturated soil.
questions.expected_answer: Some rain is intercepted by plants or evaporates; some soaks into the soil (infiltration) and reaches rivers slowly; the rest flows over the surface (surface run-off) and reaches rivers quickly. When rain is very heavy or the soil is already saturated (full of water), more rain becomes fast run-off, rivers rise rapidly and overflow their banks onto floodplains.

questions.question: Explain how four human activities make floods worse.
questions.expected_answer: Clearing vegetation and draining wetlands reduces interception and infiltration; overgrazing and ploughing downhill strip grass and compact soil; fires leave bare, hard soil; urbanisation covers land with impermeable roofs, roads and paving and storm drains speed water to rivers; building on floodplains places people in the path of floods; litter blocks drains.

questions.question: Describe five effects of floods, using South African examples where possible.
questions.expected_answer: Loss of life and injury (over 400 deaths in KZN in April 2022, many by drowning); disease such as cholera, typhoid and diarrhoea from contaminated water; displacement of tens of thousands of people; damage to buildings and infrastructure (roads, bridges, the port of Durban, power lines, water works); damage to fields, crops and livestock; soil erosion and silting of dams.
